title: Quantum resonance-enhanced performance of quantum battery
authors: Ankita Mazumdar, Shashi C. L. Srivastava, Sanku Paul
abstract: Quantum resonance arising whenever the ratio of the intrinsic system frequency to the driving frequency becomes a rational number has been demonstrated to generate super-linear entanglement, enhance transport, quantum metrology performance and communication. Here, we demonstrate that quantum resonance can also serve as a powerful resource for quantum batteries. We model the batteries as free rotors charged via a kicked protocol. When the individual batteries are at resonance, we show both analytically and numerically that charging power increases linearly with time while efficiency (defined as the fraction of stored energy that can be extracted) remains near unity despite strong entanglement generation. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this enhanced performance persists at higher-order resonances. Demonstrating the universality of this mechanism, we show that similar enhancements arise in the interacting kicked top model, and briefly note the feasibility of its experimental realization. In a broader context, resonant charging holds significant implications for energy storage, quantum computational resources, and quantum thermodynamics.
summary: The paper demonstrates that exploiting quantum resonance can dramatically boost the performance of quantum batteries, allowing them to charge power linearly over time while maintaining near-perfect energy efficiency. This enhancement is robust and persists even when strong entanglement builds up within the coupled system models.
main_problem: The study investigates whether quantum resonance can enhance the performance of quantum batteries, specifically aiming for stable charging power increase with time and near-unity efficiency despite strong entanglement generation.
main_result: Quantum resonance leads to a linear increase in charging power and maintains near-unity energy extraction efficiency ($\eta \approx 1$) even when significant entanglement is generated. This enhancement mechanism is shown to be universal across different models.
method: The authors use analytical derivations involving Bessel functions and numerical simulations to calculate stored energy, extractable work (ergotropy), and efficiency for coupled quantum rotor and kicked top systems.
model_or_system: The system models quantum batteries using free rotors or interacting kicked tops. The dynamics are governed by time-periodic Hamiltonians incorporating both intrinsic quadratic terms ($H_0$) and nonlinear interaction/kicking potentials ($V(x_1, x_2)$).
key_observables: Stored Energy ($E(	au)$), Extractable Work (Ergotropy $\xi(	au)$), Efficiency ($\eta(	au) = \xi/	ext{stored energy}$), and Linear Entropy ($S_L(	au)$ for entanglement).
important_parameters: Quantum Resonance condition (rational ratio of intrinsic to driving frequency); specific resonance conditions like $\hbar s T = 4\pi$ or $K_2 \gg K$.
main_assumptions: The analysis often relies on approximations for large time ($	au$) and specific parameter limits, such as the regime where one interaction strength dominates ($K_2 \gg K$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate linear growth of charging power at resonance (Fig. 1a), efficiency remaining near unity under resonance (Fig. 1b), and confirmation of this effect in higher-order resonances for both rotor and kicked top models.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the model using free rotors, deriving analytical results showing linear power growth at resonance. It then generalizes this to an interacting kicked top model, confirming the universality of the enhancement mechanism across different physical realizations.
why_interesting: This work connects fundamental concepts from quantum thermodynamics (energy storage/extraction) with phenomena arising from periodically driven systems (quantum resonance), providing a concrete resource for energy management in quantum technologies.
